messages.content: Write the charter for a newly formed platform engineering team. Around 250 words.

Assumes a typical in-house team serving product engineers; tell me your org's specifics and I'll tailor the scope and metrics.

---

## Platform Engineering Charter

### Why we exist

Product teams spend too much of their time on work that is not their product: wiring up CI, guessing at Kubernetes manifests, chasing an on-call page into infrastructure they did not build. We take that work off them. Our customers are the engineers inside this company, and we treat them as customers, not as tickets.

### What we own

The paved road from a commit to production traffic: build and release pipelines, environment provisioning, service scaffolding, secrets and identity plumbing, and the observability that tells a team whether their change worked. We own the defaults. Teams can step off the road, but they carry the pager when they do.

### How we work

We build products, not projects. Anything we ship has an owner, documentation a new hire can follow, and a plan for its retirement. We prefer a boring tool that people already know over a clever one we would have to teach. We do not accept work by decree; if a request does not reduce load for more than one team, it belongs in a consulting engagement, not in the platform.

### How we will know it is working

Time from empty repository to a service serving production traffic. Change failure rate and time to restore, measured across the teams we serve, not for ourselves. Adoption we did not have to mandate.

### What we are not

We are not an approval gate, a ticket queue, or the team of last resort for everyone else's outage.

### How we work

Platform work is product work, so everything we ship has a named owner, docs a new hire can follow in their first week, and a date we expect to turn it off. A dull tool the team already knows beats a sharp one we would have to teach. We do not take assignments by decree. If a request only helps one team, it is consulting work, not platform work.

### How we will know it worked

Time from an empty repo to a service taking production traffic. Change failure rate and restore time across the teams we serve, not our own. Adoption nobody had to mandate.
